CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFQUERY

CFQUERY sends the SQL between its start and end tags to a data source. A SELECT statement returns a query object you can loop over with CFOUTPUT or CFLOOP; INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and CREATE TABLE statements simply run. CFML expressions inside the tag body are evaluated before the SQL is sent, so you can build statements from form fields and variables.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFQUERY NAME="query_name"
    DATASOURCE="ds_name"
    DBTYPE="ODBC"
    MAXROWS="number"
    CACHEDWITHIN="timespan"
    CACHEDAFTER="date">
  SQL statements
</CFQUERY>

Attributes

NAME
Optional. Name of the query variable that receives the result set. Must begin with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores. Required if you want to read the results.
DATASOURCE
Required. Name of a data source registered in the KoldFusion Administrator, for example cfsnippets.
DBTYPE
Optional, default "ODBC". Driver type: ODBC, OLEDB, Oracle73, Oracle80, Sybase11, Informix73 or DB2. All of them reach the same built-in engine in KoldFusion. DBTYPE="query" (query of queries) arrived in a later version and is rejected.
MAXROWS
Optional. Maximum number of rows to keep in the result set.
CACHEDWITHIN
Optional. A time span created with CreateTimeSpan. If an identical query (same name, data source and SQL) ran within that span, the cached result is returned without contacting the database.
CACHEDAFTER
Optional. A date. A cached result is reused if it was created after this date.

Usage

After the query runs, each result set exposes the variables query_name.RecordCount, query_name.ColumnList and query_name.CurrentRow. The variable CFQUERY.ExecutionTime holds the number of milliseconds the last query took.

Text values in WHERE clauses need single quotes; single quotes inside CFML variables are doubled automatically. Use CFQUERYPARAM to bind typed values safely.

The maximum number of cached queries is set on the Caching page of the Administrator.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- List the engineers, newest first --->
<CFQUERY NAME="GetEngineers" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT FirstName, LastName, StartDate
FROM Employees
WHERE Department = 'Engineering'
ORDER BY StartDate DESC
</CFQUERY>

<H3>Engineering department</H3>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>The query returned #GetEngineers.RecordCount# rows
in #CFQUERY.ExecutionTime# ms. Columns: #GetEngineers.ColumnList#</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
<UL>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetEngineers">
  <LI>#FirstName# #LastName#, since #DateFormat(StartDate, "mmmm d, yyyy")#
</CFOUTPUT>
</UL>
